title: Complete the rooftop garden record
instructions: Read the complete passage first. Each gap changes or matches an anchor word already present. Enter exactly one word in every gap, then check the passage as one group.

parts.prompt: Gap 1: use the past-tense form of “meets” required by “during the previous term”.

response.rationale: “During the previous term” places the repeated action in the past, and the irregular past form of “meet” is “met”.

parts.hint: Find the present-tense anchor “meets”, then follow the past-time expression.
parts.correct_explanation: “Met” is the irregular past-tense form required for the club’s previous schedule.

parts.prompt: Gap 2: use the plural form of “planter” required after “four more”.

response.rationale: The number “four” requires a plural count noun, so “planter” takes the plural ending to become “planters”.

parts.hint: The passage changes from one planter to four more of the same object.

parts.prompt: Gap 3: use the present-tense form that matches “the club leader” and parallels “checks”.

response.rationale: The singular subject “the club leader” controls both coordinated verbs, so the second verb repeats the third-person singular form “checks”.

parts.hint: The verbs on both sides of “and” share the same singular subject.
parts.correct_explanation: “Checks” agrees with the singular subject and forms a parallel pair with the earlier “checks”.

parts.prompt: Gap 4: use the past participle of “drains” after the auxiliary “had”.

response.rationale: The auxiliary “had” requires a past participle, so the regular verb “drain” becomes “drained”.

parts.hint: Complete the past-perfect verb phrase “had already ___”.
parts.correct_explanation: “Had drained” is the past-perfect form describing an action completed before the students arrived.

parts.prompt: Gap 5: use the comparative form of “bright” required by “even” and “than before”.

response.rationale: “Even” and “than before” establish a comparison, so the one-syllable adjective “bright” takes “-er”.

parts.correct_explanation: “Brighter” is the comparative form that completes “even brighter than before”.

parts.prompt: Gap 6: use the noun related to “grew” after “their unexpected”.

response.rationale: The possessive determiner “their” and adjective “unexpected” require a noun, and the noun related to “grow/grew” is “growth”.

parts.hint: The phrase needs the name of the result of growing, not another verb.
parts.correct_explanation: “Growth” is the noun describing how the seedlings grew.

parts.prompt: Gap 7: use the plural noun formed from “measure” to name the recorded results.

response.rationale: “These” and the plural verb “help” require a plural noun; the recorded results of measuring are “measurements”.

parts.hint: The students measure several plants, and “these” refers to the results they record.
parts.correct_explanation: “Measurements” is the plural noun that agrees with “these” and “help”.

parts.prompt: Gap 8: use the reflexive pronoun that agrees with the plural noun “students”.

response.rationale: After “by”, the reflexive pronoun refers back to the plural subject “the students”, so the agreeing form is “themselves”.

parts.hint: The students arrange the schedule without someone else doing it for them.
parts.correct_explanation: “Themselves” agrees with the plural human referent “the students”.
